title: Chocolate supplement recalled over erectile dysfunction drug
summary: USALESS.COM is recalling its Rhino Choco VIP 10X product due to the undeclared presence of Tadalafil, which is the active ingredient in Cialis.

title: How safe is America from polio?
summary: After decades of American children routinely receiving polio vaccines, the virus that had doomed many to paralysis was nearly eliminated in the United States. But vaccine avoidance today may allow the crippling disease to return.

title: As nursing homes face staffing crisis, robots help workers focus on care
summary: A growing, aging population and an acute caregiver shortage are pushing adult care centers to think outside the box. Itay Hod introduces a new, high-tech helper.

title: Measles cases at university in Florida soar to nearly 60
summary: Twenty one states in the U.S. have confirmed cases of measles.

title: "The Great Influenza" author John M. Barry on "The Takeout" — 5/29/2020
summary: "The Great Influenza" author John M. Barry compares the COVID-19 pandemic with the deadly 1918 Spanish Flu outbreak and explains how American troops carried that earlier virus into Europe during World War I, on this week's episode of "The Takeout with Major Garrett."

title: Major Garrett sits down (remotely) with former FEMA administrator Craig Fugate on "The Takeout"
summary: Amid social distancing, Major Garrett and former FEMA Administrator Craig Fugate meet remotely to discuss the federal coronavirus response efforts and whether the Trump administration has or hasn't done enough, on this week’s episode of "The Takeout."

summary: Austin, Texas Mayor Steve Adler and Provo, Utah Mayor Michelle Kaufusi join Major to talk about how they have dealt with the coronavirus crisis on the homefront and finding the safest way to reopen, on this week"s episode of "The Takeout with Major Garrett."

title: The placebo effect
summary: Can a pill actually cure an ailment, even if that pill contains no cure? Doctors and medical researchers have discovered unexpected results from giving patients pills that aren't medicine at all. Susan Spencer reports.

title: Afghanistan midwives give a better chance at life
summary: The Afghanistan province of Badakshan was once recorded to have the world's highest maternal mortality rate. Mandy Clark reports on giving life in Afghanistan a better chance from the start.

title: Flex Spending: How to use it and not lose it
summary: How can you get the most out of a Flex Spending Account? CBS News financial contributor Carmen Wong Ulrich speaks to the "Early Show" anchors about the best ways to use a Health Care Flexible Spending Account.

title: Book excerpt: "The Let Them Theory" by Mel Robbins
summary: In her latest bestseller, the motivational speaker discusses how personal growth is only possible when you stop pouring energy into things you cannot control – which includes changing other people.

title: Extended Interview: Mel Robbins
summary: In this web exclusive, author and podcaster Mel Robbins talks with Norah O'Donnell about "The Let Them Theory."

title: Patients are being hit with this surprise fee just for seeing their doc
summary: One patient reports getting stuck with a $2,418 "facility fee" after seeing her doctor. "I didn't even know such a thing existed," she said.

title: Carter Center reaches major milestone in quest to eradicate Guinea worm
summary: Jimmy Carter made eradicating the Guinea worm a top mission of The Carter Center. Now it could soon become the second disease eradicated in history.

title: Life expectancy in U.S. hit record high of 79 years in 2024, CDC says
summary: U.S. life expectancy rose to 79 years in 2024 - the highest mark in American history. But the U.S. still ranks below dozens of other countries.

title: American Academy of Pediatrics releases vaccine recommendations that differ from CDC guidance
summary: The American Academy of Pediatrics released its own recommendations for childhood vaccinations Monday. The list differs significantly from the reduced vaccine schedule released earlier this month by the CDC. Dr. Amanda Kravitz, pediatrician at Weill Cornell in New York City, joins CBS News to discuss.

title: Dermatologist shares tips to help dry winter skin
summary: Dr. Rachel Nazarian, a board-certified dermatologist, joins "CBS Mornings" to share her tips for saving your dry winter skin.

title: Tylenol not linked to autism, new study shows, contradicting Trump administration claims
summary: A review of studies published in The Lancet found no link between acetaminophen use during pregnancy and autism, contradicting the Trump administration's recent claims.

title: Doctor on challenges in public health and impact: "The biggest problem is the confusion"
summary: Dr. Ezekiel Emanuel is an oncologist, professor and helped to write the Affordable Care Act. He speaks to "CBS Mornings" about confusion over changes to public health guidelines, living a fulfilling life and his new book, "Eat Your Ice Cream: Six Simple Rules for a Long and Healthy Life.

title: Nurses strike begins in New York City as thousands walk off jobs
summary: The largest nurses strike ever in New York City is underway as thousands of NYSNA members walk off their jobs at major hospitals.

title: NYC nurses strike looms as negotiations pass midnight deadline
summary: The potential for a major nurses strike in New York City is growing by the minute, with major hospitals and the New York State Nurses Association failing to get a deal done before Sunday's midnight deadline.

title: "Enough": Oprah Winfrey on her weight-loss lessons
summary: Oprah Winfrey is one of the best-known, most-admired and successful people on the planet. But for years she seemed powerless to conquer her fluctuating weight problem … until new medications, and a new attitude about her weight, gave her a breakthrough, which she describes in "Enough," a new book she has co-written with Dr. Ania Jastreboff. title: State of denial: How insurance companies impact health care today
summary: As millions of Americans struggle with paying for health care, doctors and health experts discuss how medical care is being eroded by insurers denying necessary tests and treatment, making it "more difficult to be healthy in the United States."

title: Book excerpt: "Enough" by Dr. Ania Jastreboff and Oprah Winfrey
summary: The media superstar, who has struggled with weight for much of her life, and a Yale School of Medicine doctor team up for a book that examines the biology of obesity, offering a new way forward.

title: Potential health concerns with drinking water on some airlines, study finds
summary: A new study found potential health concerns with the drinking water on some airlines where you might order coffee or tea. The review was of airplane drinking water stored in onboard tanks, not bottled products. Of the 10 major airlines, Delta scored best, while JetBlue and American were the bottom two carriers.

title: Flu cases surge across U.S. as 45 states report "high or very high" virus activity
summary: There have been at least 11 million cases of the flu so far this season. As cases climb, doctor visits for the flu have hit their highest level in almost three decades, the CDC says. Skyler Henry reports.

title: CDC suggests fewer shots for kids in new vaccine recommendations
summary: The Trump administration is reducing the number of vaccines it recommends for children in the U.S. Under the new guidelines, the CDC recommends all children be vaccinated against 11 diseases, which is down from 17 immunizations. CBS News medical contributor Dr. Celine Gounder explains what to know.

title: Doctor's orders: Eat ice cream, and other tips for a long and healthy life
summary: In his new wellness book, "Eat Your Ice Cream," Dr. Ezekiel Emanuel goes beyond the basics of eating, exercise and sleep, to the importance of being happy, social engagement, and recommended behaviors (like "don't be a schmuck") that can benefit longevity.
